EYEBROW: Full Stack Developer Focused on Frontend
HERO_DESCRIPTION: I like bridging backend logic with screens that anyone can understand. I have a solid background in data research and hold an Associate's Degree in Web Development (DAW). I enjoy designing clear, modular web applications. Based in Madrid, but completely used to working in English.
P1_SUMMARY: An application built during the SheBuilds Hackathon to organize and preserve family recipes, designed for seamless one-handed navigation while cooking.
P1_PROBLEM_DESC: The hackathon challenge was to build a digital solution in record time. I chose to focus on accessibility for busy households: large typography, high contrast, and navigation zones kept within thumb-reach.
P1_BUILT_DESC: I utilized an AI-first workflow (vibecoding) with Lovable to rapidly iterate the interface, connecting the React frontend directly to Supabase for database management and user authentication.
P1_CONSTRAINT_DESC: The main technical challenge was orchestrating AI tools as a pair programmer to successfully move from a conceptual idea to a live, deployed GitHub-backed app within the intense event timeline.
P1_LEARNED_DESC: I learned to act as the creative director of my own codebase—validating infrastructure in real-time while focusing entirely on delivering a smooth UX brought to life with Framer Motion.
P2_SUMMARY: An interactive digital menu and table ordering management system built as a team project, streamlining restaurant browsing through dynamic filter controls.
P2_DECISION_DESC: Static QR menus are clumsy. As the Frontend Lead, I wanted to create a fluid single-page application (SPA) where customers could instantly explore ingredients and allergen data in real time.
P2_BUILT_DESC: I developed the user interface leveraging Angular 20 components. I structured client-side services to ensure fast navigation and clean, decoupled communication with my teammates' backend API.
P2_REFLECTION_DESC: The core technical challenge here was local storage state management, ensuring that the shopping cart data and user filter preferences persisted correctly and never fell out of sync upon page reloads.
P2_LEARNED_DESC: This project solidified my team development skills in Angular, the importance of establishing solid API contracts, and using TypeDoc to ensure a clear, well-documented frontend codebase.
P3_SUMMARY: A fullstack group platform for discovering and booking astronomical events, wrapped in an immersive deep-sky visual design.
P3_ARCH_DESC: Managing time-sensitive events requires immediacy. I took charge of the Frontend development using Angular 17, designing an engaging interface connected to a Spring Boot backend infrastructure.
P3_SECURITY_DESC: We implemented a security system based on JWT tokens to separate user roles, making sure that client, guest, and dashboard administrator views were fully secured directly from the browser.
P3_BIZ_DESC: The main hurdle during development was implementing and visually reflecting the business rule capping bookings at 10 people per user, requiring strict capacity validation controls.
P3_DESIGN_DESC: Designing a Dark Mode UI with Tailwind CSS proved that accessibility and aesthetics go hand in hand. I achieved crisp contrast ratios for mobile devices, perfect for users out in the field stargazing.
JOURNEY_TITLE: From social research to software development.
J_23_DESC: Graduated in Social Sciences (Brasília) and completed a Master's in Research at UCM. This is where I learned to analyze and interpret complex data structures.
J_24_DESC: Following my training at CareerFoundry, I went straight into real-world software engineering, writing code within international development teams.
J_25_DESC: Completed two years of official studies (DAW) at UNIR to back my practical experience with an official qualification and integrate into the local tech ecosystem.
J_26_DESC: With years of coding behind me and my formal studies completed this year, I am looking to join an established engineering team where I can add immediate value.
NOTES_TITLE: Ideas, experiments, and reflections on development.
N1_TITLE: Designing components that don't turn into chaos.
N1_DESC: My notes on keeping the UI modular, clean, and easily maintainable as the project grows.
N2_TITLE: Why a clear interface matters as much as clean code.
N2_DESC: Visual hierarchy is code too. If the user can't find the button, your backend logic achieves nothing.
N3_TITLE: What Docker taught me about deployment consistency.
N3_DESC: 'It works on my machine' is not a valid excuse. Containers eliminated a massive amount of deployment headaches.
INT_TITLE: Ready to work in remote and multicultural teams.
CONTACT_DESC: I am looking for a professional team with interesting projects where I can write clean code and grow as a developer. If you'd like to chat, feel free to drop me a line!
